name: onboarding-flow
notes: Builder C walk scenario (P3): detect(greenfield) -> scaffoldTree -> detect(resume) -> preflight.run (full mode, stubbed codex) -> gates present in state.json -> loadSettings defaults land -> floor test (reviews below floor clamps UP to the enum floor value, never below it) -> telemetry.status is disabled for reason 'consent' -> settings.write lands the interview's resolved settings for real -> a second preflight.run demonstrates degraded-claude-only mode -> phases.advance lands onboarding's exit_emits and transitions to brainstorm.

Both loadSettings steps 'ignore' the clamps array in the equality check (still real, computed values -- just not re-asserted here): the exhaustive clamp-list shape is already proven by machine/test/settings-schema.test.js; this scenario's job is proving the disk-wired behavior (the resolved *values*), not re-deriving that proof.

DO_NOT_TRACK refusal is deliberately NOT a step here: telemetry.js's enabled()/status() read process.env.DO_NOT_TRACK directly (ambient), and the OPS registry calls telemetry functions with explicit args only -- there is no per-step env-injection mechanism in mock-replay's op model, and this scenario does not add one (telemetry.js/mock-replay.js are Builder A's owned files). The DO_NOT_TRACK path is proven for real by machine/test/telemetry.test.js's withEnv()-wrapped unit tests (see 'enabled is false with reason "do_not_track"...'); this scenario cites that as its evidence rather than duplicating it under a different harness.

Both preflight.run steps 'ignore' the 'repo' field of the return value (and the whole 'preflight' block when reading state.json back): check-honesty.js's runGate takes no cwd parameter by design (preflight.js's own header comment), so preflight's git checks run against THIS REPLAY PROCESS's own ambient cwd, not $TMP/proj -- running mock-replay.js from anywhere inside the thelastskill working tree (the only supported invocation; scaffoldTree's own routingConfigPath arg above is already an absolute path specific to this checkout) makes 'preflight-git' pass deterministically, but the captured branch NAME is whatever branch happens to be checked out, which this scenario must not pin to a literal value.

The second preflight.run's 'gates' array carries SIX entries, not three: preflight.md's own State field says 'append' for every one of the five checks, so a second run's node/codex/git evidence is appended alongside the first run's, never deduplicated or overwritten by gate name -- this is also why codex-preflight's own two entries in that array legitimately carry two different 'cmd' strings ('exit 0' then 'exit 1'), one per run.

settings.write is called with an empty candidate ('{}') to demonstrate the exact same real function the onboarding interview calls once at its own end (Maestro's Bash-law onboarding-engine point) -- an empty candidate resolves to every knob's own schema default, the identical object machine/test/settings-schema.test.js already proves for an empty applySchema input, so this step doubles as an end-to-end confirmation that settings.write's clamping path is the same one, not a second one.

settings.write's args now carry a third element, {source: 'interview'} -- the floor-lock doctrine's provenance marker (operator ruling 2026-07-28 [seq 48]) that product/onboarding/flow.md's own pinned CLI invocation passes as '--source interview'; this step models that real call shape, not only its candidate/treeRoot arguments. The expect object gains floor_lock: true, the schema default -- unaffected by the source marker here since an absent floor_lock in the candidate never reaches the interview_only gate at all (that gate only fires on an actual non-default value attempt).

The settings.applySchema step immediately after demonstrates the locked-install clamp directly (rule: 'locked'), the mechanism write() itself delegates to but does not surface in its own return value (write() returns settings only, never clamps, to stay backward compatible with every existing caller) -- calling applySchema straight, on the real product schema, with override_verification_floor: true in an otherwise fully-explicit, already-at-default candidate keeps the resulting clamps array to exactly one entry (every other key is supplied at its own valid default, which never generates a clamp) rather than needing to also enumerate the full default-fill noise a {} candidate would produce; the exhaustive floor-lock clamp/message shapes are proven exactly this way by machine/test/settings-schema.test.js, this step's job is proving the exact same mechanism is reachable end-to-end via the OPS dispatcher, not re-deriving the proof.

facilitator.description: Who runs your brainstorm sessions: Opus 5 is the default collaborative thinking partner; Fable 5 is the heavyweight essayist for decisions that are expensive to redo.
facilitator.cost_note: Opus 5 — the lighter seat per session, no measured figure yet; Fable 5 — roughly 2x Opus 5 per session, no measured figure yet.

research_width.description: How many parallel researchers work under the research chief: 2 for a focused question, 3 for standard breadth-first research, 5 for the widest fan-out that still pays off.
research_width.cost_note: 2 workers — the narrowest fan-out and the cheapest of the three, no measured figure yet; 3 workers — the middle of the three, no measured figure yet; 5 workers — the widest fan-out and the most expensive, no measured figure yet (the chief seat is a fixed cost, additional under every option).

planning.description: How hard the plan is interrogated before building: Standard is one accountable draft plus a cross-family coverage check; Deep scrutiny escalates the draft and adds two adversarial cross-family passes; Maximal confrontation is the most adversarial tier available.
planning.cost_note: Standard — the baseline, no measured figure yet; Deep scrutiny — roughly 2x standard, no measured figure yet; Maximal confrontation — two full independent drafts instead of one, no measured figure yet.

reviews.description: Verification never scales down. Floor is the minimum — every chunk gets one cross-family review, every milestone a dual-model review, the journey suite always runs. x3/x5 only add aggregated reinforcement passes on top of that floor; there is no lower option.
reviews.cost_note: Floor — fixed, not shaveable, no measured figure yet; Reinforced x3 — adds independent check-again passes per chunk on top of the floor, no measured figure yet; Maximum x5 — adds more of the same per chunk, no measured figure yet.

checkpoints.description: When the pipeline stops and shows you its work: Milestone pauses stop at each milestone review with a summary and spend-so-far; Autonomous runs the whole slice end-to-end and only reviews at the finish line. Verification gates still block bad work internally either way.
checkpoints.cost_note: No direct cost difference between the two options; both run the same verification floor.

budget.description: Hard ceiling per feature slice for each model family, plus an opt-in rough-cost report from logged token usage x current API prices.
budget.cost_note: Ceiling values are operator-set dollar amounts, left at no-ceiling (null) by default pending dogfood calibration of real per-slice costs (settings-menu-design.md §6 item 7).

claude_ceiling_usd.description: Hard spend ceiling in USD for Claude-family seats on this slice. null means no ceiling.
claude_ceiling_usd.cost_note: Operator-set; no evidence-backed default dollar figure exists yet — defaults to no-ceiling (null).

codex_ceiling_usd.description: Hard spend ceiling in USD for Codex/Sol-family seats on this slice. null means no ceiling.
codex_ceiling_usd.cost_note: Operator-set; no evidence-backed default dollar figure exists yet — defaults to no-ceiling (null).

budget_report.description: Opt in to a rough cost report (logged token usage x current API prices) even when there is no ceiling — for the no-ceiling-but-curious.
budget_report.cost_note: The report itself costs nothing extra to produce; it reads the usage stream that already exists.

telemetry_consent.description: Record anonymous, content-free build statistics (phase timings, review pass counts, model routing outcomes, costs) locally under .thelastskill/usage/ to improve defaults over time. Never your code, never your prompts, never leaves your machine.
telemetry_consent.cost_note: No direct cost impact; writes a local JSONL stream only.

blocking_preference.description: When the pipeline hits a blocker: auto_remedy lets it attempt a remedy on its own (e.g. via the Agreement Pass) before asking you; advise_me always stops and asks first.
blocking_preference.cost_note: No direct cost impact; changes only who decides at a blocker.

plan_review.description: After planning completes: auto_proceed moves straight into building; review pauses so you can read the plan first.
plan_review.cost_note: No direct cost impact; changes only whether the pipeline pauses after planning.

floor_lock.source_locked_message: floor_lock cannot be hand-unlocked; only the settings interview can set it to false, and the interview asks once — a completed install is not re-asked, and a hand-edit of this key is clamped back to true.

override_verification_floor.locked_message: floor is locked in this install; override_verification_floor is inert
override_verification_floor.warn_message: override_verification_floor is active in this install — the verification floor clamp is disabled for this run.

clamps.message: floor is locked in this install; override_verification_floor is inert
